subject: economics
objective: What is GDP by the expenditure approach?
instruction: The Bureau of Westvale publishes the following for the year. (a) Spending side: household consumption USD 9,800,000, gross investment USD 2,600,000, government spending USD 3,100,000, exports USD 1,900,000 and imports USD 2,200,000. (b) Income side: net factor income from abroad is USD 400,000 and depreciation is USD 1,100,000. (c) Price and population: the GDP deflator is 110 and the population is 12,500 people. Use the expenditure method for GDP, gross national income (GNI) = GDP + net factor income from abroad, net national income (NNI) = GNI - depreciation, and real GDP = nominal GDP / GDP deflator x 100 (base year = 100). Per-person figures divide by the population. Required: gdp, net exports, gni, nni, real gdp, real nni, gdp per capita, real gdp per capita.
